audit_findings.magnitude: $378.5 million closing proceeds and $78.2 million of transferred leaseback liabilities; continuing-OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: FY2025 OE includes three months of the sold Pasta Business, while the bridge uses post-sale June 2026 cash and debt; continuing OE, proceeds and transferred liabilities must share one perimeter
audit_findings.evidence: In August 2025, we entered into an agreement to sell 8th Avenue’s pasta business (the “Pasta Business”), which is expected to close in the first quarter of fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error: the Pasta Business was sold on December 1, 2025, but the valuation records no perimeter adjustment. The direction is unresolved because pasta-specific OE is not disclosed and consolidated 8th Avenue recorded a $21.4 million operating loss during its three FY2025 months. The transaction is large enough that an unreconciled earnings-and-bridge treatment could change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Remove the Pasta Business's attributable earnings, D&A and maintenance capital from normalized OE; reconcile the $378.5 million proceeds, $4.0 million estimated working-capital payable and $78.2 million liability transfer through June 2026 cash, debt and repurchases; then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Convertible-note interest and dilution describe different equity claims
audit_findings.magnitude: 5.4 million shares, equal to 10.6% of the 51.036212 million denominator; no-conversion base value computes to $128.25 per share versus $114.69, a $13.56 or 11.8% difference, before cash-settlement effects; annual after-tax interest is $10.9 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The denominator assumes conversion while equity-level OE retains the convertible notes' interest expense, burdening common equity with both interest and full conversion dilution
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, dilutive net earnings are adjusted for interest expense, net of tax, related to the Company’s convertible senior notes.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated claim-basis inconsistency. Its scale is sufficient to move the base buy-below threshold above the $84.64 market price under the no-conversion denominator alternative, so it can change the investment conclusion. The final correction depends on expected cash, share or mixed settlement.
audit_findings.action: Rerun on two coherent bases: after-interest OE with settlement-appropriate shares and financing consequences, and 51.036212 million shares with $10.9 million of after-tax interest restored to OE; use the settlement terms and current conversion economics to select the primary case.

audit_findings.title: FY2020 consolidated cash-flow add-backs may contaminate a parent-common anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: A parent-attributable earnings starting point may have been combined with consolidated D&A, maintenance capital and other cash-flow adjustments, affecting FY2020 OE of $268.2 million and therefore the log-trend anchor
audit_findings.evidence: The remaining interest in the consolidated net earnings and net assets of Weetabix East Africa is allocated to NCI.
audit_findings.explanation: The presence of noncontrolling ownership is demonstrated, but the record does not supply the FY2020 subsidiary allocations needed to establish an error or its direction. Consolidated D&A would raise OE while consolidated capital requirements would lower it. Because FY2020 enters a sparse eight-observation trend, even a one-year mismatch may affect the $397.7 million anchor, but materiality is not presently measurable.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct FY2020 OE on a parent-common basis using subsidiary-level D&A, maintenance capital and other adjustments attributable to NCI, or exclude FY2020 and rerun the log trend and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Recent OE may embed abnormal HPAI egg pricing
audit_findings.magnitude: $269.5 million FY2025 Foodservice egg-sales increase attributed primarily to HPAI pricing, plus $22.1 million of Refrigerated Retail egg-sales growth partly from HPAI pricing; normalized OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporary HPAI pricing can inflate FY2024-FY2025 OE observations, the log-trend anchor and any growth applied to that anchor
audit_findings.evidence: Egg product sales were up $269.5 million, or 14%, primarily driven by incremental HPAI pricing (partially offset by the pass-through of lower grain costs) and 3% higher volumes.
audit_findings.explanation: Exceptional HPAI pricing is demonstrated, and the June 2026 filing confirms that later egg-price declines reflected reduced or lapped HPAI pricing. The supplied filings do not isolate the net OE benefit after egg costs, flock losses and volume effects. Nevertheless, the disclosed sales movements are large relative to the $397.7 million anchor and are reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion despite use of the lower trend anchor.
audit_findings.action: Build through-cycle Foodservice and Refrigerated Retail egg economics using normalized prices, egg costs, flock losses, replacement costs and volumes; replace the affected OE observations or apply a documented normalization adjustment and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Bob Evans restaurant lease guarantees are an unbridged senior contingent claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $13.5 million current annual rent, 3.4% of $397.7 million anchor OE; approximately $103.0 million 13-year present value at 10% with 1.5% annual escalation, equal to 1.8% of $5,853 million base equity or $2.02 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A buyer default could create senior rent payments not reflected in historical OE or the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: The current annual rent on these leases is $ 13.5 and will increase up to 1.5 % annually based on indexed inflation.
audit_findings.explanation: The guarantee is demonstrated, but no default is indicated and the filing reports protections, mitigation duties and an immaterial fair value. Even a deliberately severe proxy that capitalizes approximately 13 years of all current rent would reduce base value by about $2.02 per share and the 30%-MOS buy-below level by about $1.41, from $80.28 to roughly $78.87; it would not reverse the current no-buy conclusion at $84.64.
audit_findings.action: Retain a contingent-liability note and monitor the restaurant buyer's credit, defaults and lease amendments; rerun only if evidence indicates probable payments, material renewal exposure or loss of mitigation rights.

audit_findings.title: Signed but uncommenced leases create future costs outside historical OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $138.3 million of filed future minimum payments over 10-15 years; incremental annual OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Once commenced, warehouse rent enters operating expense and OE; treating related operating benefits as growth without the associated incremental rent would overstate forecast OE
audit_findings.evidence: As of September 30, 2025, the Company had signed lease agreements that had not yet commenced related to warehouses within our Foodservice and Refrigerated Retail segments, which had future minimum lease payments of $ 138.3 not included in the tables above.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual commitment is demonstrated, but it was forward-looking and outside FY2025 lease liabilities and historical expense. The record does not establish how much replaces existing warehouse spending, when each lease commenced, or what operating benefits accompany it, so the full $138.3 million is not an equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 lease roll-forward and warehouse transition plans, identify commenced rent and displaced third-party warehousing costs, and incorporate only the net incremental after-tax expense into forecast OE when operations begin.
